deadline_note: Set by UWC Georgia national committee. 2027-29 IBDP cycle ran 1 Aug - 30 Sep 2026 (23:59 Tbilisi) and is CLOSED. Remaining 2026 steps: video interview 31 Oct, final selection day 28 Nov (preliminary dates). Next cycle (2028 entry) not yet announced; if the pattern holds it would be Aug-Sep 2027.
eligibility_georgia: yes - Georgian citizens, or residents of Georgia attending a local school (refugees in Georgia also eligible); aged 16 or 17 on the day classes start; in secondary or post-secondary education but not yet at university; max two applications in total through UWC Georgia. Qatar: n/a (apply via Qatar's own national committee).
corrections: Deadline 2026-11-16 / opens 2026-09-08 are wrong: UWC Georgia's portal says 'Opens 1 Aug 2026' and 'Deadline 30 Sep 2026' (apply.uwc.org/prog/nc_georgia_2026).

Eligibility is age-based, not grade-based: 'Born 2009-2010, grade 10 or 11' should be replaced with 'aged 16 or 17 on the date classes start' (ge.uwc.org/eligibility-criteria). For 2027 entry that is roughly born Sep 2009 - Aug 2011.
The national committee nominates selected candidates to a UWC school; Georgians do not apply to UWC Atlantic directly. Make it clear the school is not guaranteed.
Funding: UWC Georgia says '80% of IBDP students selected by a UWC national committee receive full or partial financial support', and it is need-based. 'Up to 100%' is fine, but it is not automatic.

Student numbers differ between sources (350 vs 381 students; 75+ vs 90+ countries), so soften '350 students from 90+ countries' to 'about 350 students'. The 12th-century St Donat's Castle claim checks out.

eligibility_georgia: yes - via UWC Georgia national committee (age 16-17 at start, Georgian citizen or resident). Specific school is assigned by nomination, not chosen.
corrections: Deadline and opening dates are wrong; same as UWC Georgia national committee (opens 2026-08-01, closed 2026-09-30).
'Tuition and boarding covered for selected Georgian students' overstates it. Support is need-based ('80% ... receive full or partial financial support'), per ge.uwc.org.
Eligibility is 'age 16 or 17 when classes begin', not 'grade 10-11'.
All students study Italian and the college has students from 80+ countries, so those claims hold. 'Extensive UN and diplomacy programming' could not be verified.

deadline_note: Set by UWC Georgia national committee; 2027 entry cycle CLOSED (1 Aug - 30 Sep 2026).
eligibility_georgia: yes - via UWC Georgia national committee (age 16-17 at start).
corrections: Deadline and opening dates are wrong; same as UWC Georgia NC (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-30).

Could not find support for 'Refugee and humanitarian scholarship tracks'. The documented feature is Red Cross service work, including work with refugees and with adults with physical or mental disabilities. Selection is funded by Nordic public funding and is 'based entirely on merit and potential'.
Could not find support for 'Marine biology and Arctic environmental science'. Remove it or replace with the fjord-side outdoor setting, which is documented.
Eligibility is 'aged 16-17', not 'Grade 10-11'.

deadline_note: Set by UWC Georgia national committee; 2027 entry cycle CLOSED (1 Aug - 30 Sep 2026). UWC-USA's own admissions page: https://www.uwc-usa.org/admissions/
eligibility_georgia: yes - via UWC Georgia national committee (age 16-17 at start).
corrections: Deadline and opening dates are wrong (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-30 via UWC Georgia NC).

The Davis UWC Scholars Program is open to graduates of all 18 UWC schools, not just UWC-USA. It has 106 partner institutions for 2025-26, so '90+' is outdated (davisuwcscholars.org; Vassar news, Feb 2026).

UWC-USA's site does not mention a 'Bilingual Spanish-English environment', so remove it. The site does document the Wilderness Program and the 'Constructive Engagement of Conflict' commitment, with students from 80 countries.
'Strongest US university pipeline in the UWC movement' is an unsourced superlative.

deadline_note: Official (American Councils Georgia): applications for 2027-28 accepted through 22 Oct 2026, now CLOSED ('აპლიკაციების მიღება დასრულებულია'). Next cycle (2028-29) is expected to recruit in fall 2027.
eligibility_georgia: yes - Georgia is a FLEX Global country for 2027-28. Must be a Georgian citizen, born 1 Jan 2010 - 31 Dec 2011, in grade 9, 10 or 11, not have lived in the US more than 90 days in the last 5 years, and meet US visa requirements. Qatar: not a FLEX Global country.
corrections: The programme is now 'FLEX Global' (it merges FLEX and YES), funded by US State Dept ECA and run by American Councils with AFS, Amideast and iEARN. discoverflex.org redirects to discoverflexglobal.org.

Selection order is wrong. Per American Councils Georgia it has three rounds: Round 1 is personal info plus 3 essays (online); Round 2 is a short 15-minute English test; Round 3 is a parent meeting, English testing, extra essays, the application and an interview. It does not start with an English test in your city.

Coverage: round-trip travel, monthly allowance, host family, US school enrolment, orientation, and medical insurance (excluding pre-existing conditions and dental care). Not covered: passport costs, excess baggage, data plans (2027-28 brochure).
Eligibility should give the exact birthdate window (1 Jan 2010 - 31 Dec 2011) instead of 'born within the announced age window'.

deadline_note: Set per consortium/programme. EU: 'Most master's programmes require applications to be submitted between October and January' for the following year. There is no single deadline, so 2027-01-15 is a placeholder.
eligibility_georgia: yes - 'Students from all over the world are welcome'. Need a bachelor's degree, or be in the final year and graduate before the master's starts.
corrections: 'One application can cover several consortia' is wrong. You apply directly to each programme: 'Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme' (erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu).
Programme count: the official catalogue currently lists 218 projects, so 'Over 150' is outdated ('200+' would be accurate).
Stipend: 'up to EUR 1,400 per month' (secondary source: Mendel University page). EU pages only say scholarships cover participation costs and contribute to travel, visa and living costs.
The deadline should be null or per-programme, not 2027-01-15.

deadline_note: Individuals do not apply to the EU and have no central deadline; they join a project run by an organisation. Organisations apply to National Agencies by 12 February (projects starting 1 Jun - 31 Dec) and 1 October (projects starting 1 Jan - 31 May next year), 12:00 Brussels time, per the current Programme Guide. 2026-12-04 has no basis.
eligibility_georgia: yes - Georgia is a 'third country not associated to the Programme', Region 2 (Neighbourhood East). It can take part in youth exchanges with EU/associated-country organisations. The applicant organisation must be based in an EU Member State or associated country, and Georgian participants join through a partner organisation.
corrections: Ages 13-30 and duration 5-21 days are confirmed ('From 5 to 21 days, excluding travel days').
The 2026-12-04 deadline and 2026-09-01 opening date are invented. Replace them with 'rolling, via partner organisations; organisational rounds 12 Feb / 1 Oct'.
'Programme countries' is outdated wording. The EU now says 'EU Member States and third countries associated to the Programme'.
Group leaders must be 18+.

deadline_note: Set by the student's home university international office. There is no central application ('Contact your university's international or Erasmus+ office'), so 2027-02-28 is a placeholder.
eligibility_georgia: yes, conditionally - only if the Georgian home university has an inter-institutional agreement with the host (e.g., a Polish university) under international credit mobility. Georgia is a non-associated third country.
corrections: 'Credits transfer automatically under ECTS' is misleading. Recognition is defined in a learning agreement signed before departure, and the sending institution must then recognise the credits.
Duration: 'minimum of 2 months to a maximum of 12 months' per study cycle. '1-2 semesters' is roughly right.
'At least one completed year' is not an EU-level rule (the page does not require it). It may be a home-university rule.
The grant is 'a contribution to your travel and daily living costs'. 'Covering most living costs' overstates it. Tuition at the host is waived.
The fixed city list (Warsaw, Krakow, Wroclaw) depends on each Georgian university's partner agreements.

deadline_note: Official: Regular Decision (Applicant Pool #2) deadline 11:59pm ET, 6 Jan 2027. Early Action (Pool #1) was 15 Oct 2026 and has passed.
eligibility_georgia: yes - 'YYGS accepts applications from all countries', and need-based aid is available to all countries. Must be a current high school sophomore or junior (or international equivalent) graduating in 2028 or 2029 (Northern Hemisphere), and aged 16-18 by 18 July 2027.
corrections: 'Six academic tracks from Applied Science to Politics, Law & Economics' is wrong. There are 3 tracks: Innovations in Science & Technology (IST), Politics, Law & Economics (PLE), and Solving Global Challenges (SGC), offered in 3 two-week sessions (Jun 20 - Jul 2, Jul 4 - Jul 16, Jul 18 - Jul 30).
Age: '16 to 18 years old by July 18, 2027', not '16+ by the session'.
Aid is 'a tuition discount (up to 100% of tuition)'. The official site does not say 'Early deadline gives the best aid odds'. It says aid must be requested in the main application.
The deadline 2027-01-10 should be 2027-01-06. 'Seminar groups of fifteen' could not be verified.

deadline_note: Not published. LSE says 'Applications for Summer School 2027 will open in late November' (2026). 2026 applications are closed.
eligibility_georgia: yes for university students - no nationality restriction stated. NOT for current grade 11 school students: 100-level courses need proof of a university offer or a university transcript; 200/300-level courses need a university transcript. Target grades around B+ (GPA 3.3), plus English language evidence.
corrections: Grades '11-12' / 'Age 17+' is wrong. Applicants must be university students or hold a university offer (LSE 'Minimum requirements').
The opening date 2026-11-01 should be 'late November 2026'. The deadline 2027-04-30 is unsourced.
2027 sessions are 3 weeks each: 14 Jun - 2 Jul, 5 - 23 Jul, 26 Jul - 13 Aug 2027. More than 100 courses.

'Scholarships for students from partner regions' is wrong. LSE offers Academic Director's Scholarships for promise in Sustainability and Development, Responsible Leadership, and Technology, Media & Society.
Credit: LSE says 'Earn credit towards your degree' (transfer is decided by the home university). It is taught by LSE faculty.

deadline_note: Unverifiable: the official ETH SSRF page publishes no 2027 dates. 2026-12-15 has no official source.
eligibility_georgia: yes - 'open to all students worldwide, except for students enrolled at ETH Zurich'; undergraduate and graduate students.
corrections: Duration: 'takes place during two summer months', not '8-12 weeks'.

Eligibility is not limited to 'Second-year undergraduates and above in CS, maths or engineering'. It is open to undergraduate and graduate students worldwide (not ETH students). Research areas are CS (ML, security, systems, robotics, PL/SE, bio/medical informatics, HCI, theory, visual computing).
Stipend, travel allowance and accommodation are not stated on the official page, so the 'Monthly stipend plus travel allowance' highlight is unverified.
URL should be the D-INFK SSRF page, not the ethz.ch homepage.

deadline_note: Programme-specific ('Please refer to the specific programs for information on application deadlines'). For the winter semester, international applicants need uni-assist preliminary documentation 'before 15.07.' 2027-01-15 is unsourced.
eligibility_georgia: yes, with conditions - Georgian school certificates may not qualify directly; check DAAD/anabin. Georgians are non-EU, so they PAY tuition fees.
corrections: MAJOR: TUM is NOT tuition-free for Georgian (non-EU/EEA) students. Since winter semester 2024/25, bachelor's fees are 'usually 2,000 or 3,000 euros per semester'. From winter semester 2027/28 they rise to EUR 2,300 or 3,400 per semester. Fee waivers and scholarships are available on application (tum.de/en/studies/fees/tuition).
'Semester contribution of roughly EUR 150' is incomplete. It is paid on top of tuition and 'varies depending on the campus location'.

'Georgian school leavers usually need a Studienkolleg year first' is unverified. TUM says some foreign certificates do not qualify directly and refers to DAAD/anabin. It does not state Georgia's status.
Rename 'TUM - Tuition-Free Bachelor's' and change cost from 'tuition-free' to 'paid'.

deadline_note: Official: international admissions for September 2027 'will close on 1 March 2027, 11:59pm (Paris time)'. Currently open.
eligibility_georgia: yes - international (foreign secondary diploma) route. Must be sitting final exams in the current year (recent graduates within 12 months may apply by exception). One application only; oral examination before a jury.
corrections: MAJOR: income-based tuition does NOT apply to non-EU students. Students whose parents' tax residence is outside the EEA pay a fixed EUR 14,900/year (2026-27). The EUR 0-14,900 income scale applies to French/EU/EEA students only. Remove 'Income-based tuition applies to international students too' and 'drops to zero for lower-income international families'.
The deadline 2027-02-26 should be 2027-03-01.

Dual degrees: confirmed that Columbia, UC Berkeley, UCL and Keio are among 11 international dual bachelor's partners (others: FU Berlin, FGV EAESP, LUISS, NUS, UBC, HKU, Sydney). Dual degrees are applied for through partner portals and are longer than 3 years.
Interview: the official page says candidates must 'convince a jury during the oral examination', so this is confirmed.
The 3-year programme with the third year abroad is confirmed ('Two years in France and one year abroad').

deadline_note: Unverifiable: NUS OAM pages are behind a bot/CAPTCHA check and could not be read. 2027-02-21 is unconfirmed.

corrections: Could not verify the scholarship names, coverage, 'Tuition grant scheme cuts fees substantially for all internationals' (historically the MOE Tuition Grant carries a service obligation to work in Singapore), or 'SAT/ACT or A-Levels' requirements. Verify manually in a normal browser.
The 'ASEAN' wording in the title is likely misleading for a Georgian audience (inferred from the scholarship name, not checked against the official page).

'MEXT-linked scholarship routes' and 'Scholarships cover tuition and a monthly allowance' are unverified. The official English page documents a JPY 150,000/month scholarship only for GSC (transfer students).

corrections: The official name was 'KAIST International Summer School (KISS)', not 'International Summer Session'. No evidence it currently runs.
Eligibility did NOT include high-school seniors; it was for undergraduate and graduate students only.

'Partial scholarships for partner-country students' was really a tuition exemption only for nominees from partner universities with an exchange imbalance.

Students already in post-secondary study, or starting in Jan 2027, are ineligible.

deadline_note: Official cycles (page not year-labelled; for Fall 2027): Early Action (binding optional) 1 Nov; Regular Decision I 5 Jan; Regular Decision II 2 Mar. Financial aid deadlines are one week later. Next is 2026-11-01; the final one is 2027-03-02.
eligibility_georgia: yes - 'All students, regardless of citizenship, are eligible to apply for financial aid.'
corrections: 'Seven Cities' / 'seven cities on four continents' is outdated. Minerva now says 'Four Years, Four Cities': San Francisco (yr 1), Tokyo (yr 2), Buenos Aires and a European city (yrs 3-4); current options include Berlin. Past cities included Hyderabad, Seoul and Taipei.

corrections: MAJOR: 'Georgia is an eligible country' is false for the current (2026) cycle.

corrections: MAJOR: 'Ashinaga Africa & Eurasia Initiative' does not exist. The programme is the Ashinaga Africa Initiative (AAI) and Georgians are ineligible.
Must 'Have lost one or both parents' (confirmed). An age limit of 'under 22' is not stated on the official page.

Study destination is now universities in France (Francophone track), with an online Orientation Program from Oct to Dec and a Study Camp. 'Preparatory year in Tokyo, Paris or Kampala' is not supported.

Recommend removing from a Georgia-facing database.

deadline_note: No separate scholarship deadline. Automatic consideration once you receive an offer; deadlines are those of the course application.
eligibility_georgia: yes for the Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship (Georgia is on the official list of countries with GDP per capita of US$10,000 or less). NO for the Chancellor's Scholarship (domestic only). Qatar: not on the eligible list.
corrections: MAJOR: the Melbourne Chancellor's Scholarship exists but is DOMESTIC ONLY. It is for Australian/NZ citizens or permanent residents with an Australian Year 12/IB and ATAR 99.90+. It is not an 'international entry award' and does not cover international full tuition.

The correct international equivalent for Georgians is the Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarship: 'From 2027, the scholarships provides a 20 per cent fee sponsorship for the duration of the course and the number of scholarships will increase to 225' (25% for awards before 2027). It is automatic, ranked on final secondary results, for citizens of listed countries (Georgia included).
Replace 'full tuition plus an annual living allowance' with '20% tuition fee remission'.
'Post-study work rights of 2-4 years' was not checked here (it is an Australian government rule, not a University rule).

deadline_note: Rolling: 'Nominations are open year-round', but only in recruiting countries. 2027-05-30 is unsourced.
eligibility_georgia: no - 'You can only apply to AYC in the country that you are a resident of. Currently, the AYC program is recruiting for Nigeria, Brazil, India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, and the United States.' Qatar: no.
corrections: MAJOR: not open to Georgian residents. Ashoka says to 'write to your Ashoka country office for youth-related opportunities' instead.
Age: 'You are under 20 years of age', not '12-20'.
'Funding for the idea' is not mentioned by Ashoka. The programme is a network and selection process; panel-related travel costs are reimbursed. Remove 'fully-funded' and 'funding'.
Selection runs in four stages: online nomination, national review, international review, and an in-person selection panel.
